title: Claim take-over and fence-lost interrupts do not lapse the dead drive's spend holds
instrument: job.test.ts case: a corpse drive with a live-mode producer that reserves under JOB_USD then hangs; a second runJob takes the slot over; count spend_reservations state='held' for the corpse owner (expect 0, today 1). Needs RunOptions.spendClasses and workers/worker.ts passing [JOB_USD] (out of scope).
body:
## Summary
Only `recover` lapses a dead owner's held spend reservations; the two other interrupt paths in packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts do not.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts:377 `recover` calls `lapseOwner(t, cls, spendOwner(lease.holder))` for each spend class before `interrupt`. The claim's take-over sweep (packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts:180, `interrupt(t, orphan, holder, "lane-taken-over")`) and `settleError`'s fence-lost branch (packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts:224) interrupt the same kind of orphan without lapsing, because RunOptions has no `spendClasses`. A reservation of a dead drive found that way stays `held` forever (packages/kernel/src/spend/ledger.ts:316; only v1Port expires holds) - it still counts against the class, but reads as an in-flight call and is never aged as `lapsed`. job-core.ts:94-97 documents the lapse as the rule for every dead drive. Fixed: RunOptions.spendClasses, lapsed in `interrupt` itself, the worker passing its classes.

## Flow
- a live job's drive reserves under JOB_USD and its process dies
- a CLI runJob claims the slot after the TTL: take-over interrupts the orphan
- spend_reservations row stays state='held' with the dead owner

## Expected impact
Spend view shows a phantom in-flight call per take-over; the class's lapse counters undercount dead drives. Could break: double lapse if recover later sees the same owner (lapseOwner selects only held rows, so idempotent).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every interrupt of a dead drive lapses its holds
Before: 1 of 3 interrupt paths lapses (read: job-run.ts:180, :224, :377)
After: 3 of 3 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked the three paths; the instrument needs a RunOptions field and a workers/worker.ts edit outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts:180 interrupt(t, orphan, holder, "lane-taken-over") - no lapse
packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts:224 interrupt(t, job, holder, `fence-lost: ${loss}`) - no lapse
packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts:377 for (const cls of opts.spendClasses ?? []) lapseOwner(...)
workers/worker.ts:295 spendClasses: [JOB_USD] (workLoop only)

title: Python lease acquire re-raises past its deadline without leaving the queue
instrument: a case beside packages/kernel/py/lease_spec.py (or lease.mixed.test.ts): queue once, then make the claim raise 'database is locked' after the deadline; count lease_waiters rows (expect 0).
body:
## Summary
packages/kernel/py/lease.py `acquire` has the defect 98d4de7f fixed in the Node half: a store-busy error past the deadline re-raises with the queued ticket still in lease_waiters.

## Description
packages/kernel/py/lease.py:363-368 re-raises the OperationalError when time.monotonic() >= deadline, without `leave_in`, after an earlier poll may have queued the ticket. The ticket's holder (this Python process) is alive, so `decideClaim` counts it ahead of every newcomer until its TTL. packages/kernel/src/lease.ts now leaves on that path (98d4de7f). Out of this context's paths (kernel-python-protocol).

## Flow
- Python forge acquire(gpu.local, wait_s=600) queues behind a Node holder
- store busy past busy_timeout after the deadline
- raise without leave_in: the ticket stays; Node drives read busy up to 120 s

## Expected impact
GPU lane blocked up to a TTL after a Python waiter gives up. Could break: nothing; leave_in is idempotent.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - parity with the Node acquire
Before: Node 1/1 error paths leave; Python 0/1
After: 1/1 both
Method: simulation - read side by side; Python is another context's path
Result: better
Gate: none

title: worker-lanes.test.ts --once cases time out at vitest's 5 s: the runner's cold start alone is 5.5 s
instrument: run tests/next-server/worker-lanes.test.ts 5x alone and 1x beside the full unit lane; count the two --once cases' timeouts before/after a per-test timeout of 60 s (spawnSync already allows 120 s).
body:
## Summary
The two --once cases in tests/next-server/worker-lanes.test.ts spawn workers/runner.mts with spawnSync but run under vitest's default 5 s test timeout; the process's start-up alone takes ~5.5 s on this box.

## Description
tests/next-server/worker-lanes.test.ts:78 and :92 call `runner()` (spawnSync, timeout 120_000) inside `it(...)` with no timeout argument. Measured: `node workers/runner.mts --help` real 5.56 s. Runs alone: 1 of 4 runs failed both cases (7.3 s, 7.2 s), 3 of 4 passed; under the targeted run beside three other next-server files both failed (8.7 s, 9.9 s). Not caused by this context: with packages/kernel/src/job-worker.ts at its pre-round version the suite also passes or fails by load. Fix: a 60 s timeout on the two cases (the spawn's own bound is 120 s). Subject is workers/ + tests/next-server, outside this context.

## Flow
- vitest starts the case (5 s budget)
- spawnSync node workers/runner.mts imports the producers registry: 5.5 s cold
- the case times out although the runner would have answered

## Expected impact
Removes the recurring every-wave flake from the unit lane. Could break: nothing; a hung runner is still bounded by spawnSync's 120 s.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a flaky gate stops flaking
Before: 2 of 5 cases red in 2 of 5 runs (both --once cases); runner cold start 5.56 s
After: 0 timeouts predicted with a 60 s case timeout
Method: probe - timed the bare runner and re-ran the file 4x; the fix is a test file outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
time node workers/runner.mts --help -> real 0m5.560s
worker-lanes.test.ts: x a head no binding reaches ... 8767ms / 7321ms; x a head on a lane outside --lanes ... 9938ms / 7246ms
same file green 3 of 4 runs

title: A pause then resume during one step settles the producer as stopped while the job is queued
instrument: job.settle.test.ts case: gated step; pause and resume while it runs; assert settle is not told 'stopped' for a job whose state is queued (today told ['queued','stopped']).
body:
## Summary
packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts reports `stopped` from its `claim`/`idle` branch, and job-settle.ts tells the producer `stopped`, even when the job was resumed mid-step and is back in the queue.

## Description
An operator pause drops the record's lease (job.ts `pause`), a resume makes it `queued`; the drive's next decision (packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts:289-292) is `claim`, reports outcome `stopped`, and `endingOf` (packages/kernel/src/job-settle.ts:49) passes `stopped` to `settle`. A producer that copies endings onto a v1 store (extract run.json, an article run) writes stopped for a job that will run again. Fixed: report `yielded` (no ending) when the job read at the boundary is queued.

## Flow
- step a in flight
- operator pause, then resume
- drive boundary: decision claim -> outcome stopped -> settle('stopped')
- job queued; next drive finishes and settles done

## Expected impact
Producer stores briefly read stopped for a live job. Could break: worker reports that treat stopped as WAITING (workers/worker.ts) - check.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - settle is told only real endings
Before: pause+resume mid-step: settle told stopped (walked)
After: no settle call; outcome yielded
Method: simulation - walked job.ts pause/resume, job-run.ts:289, job-settle.ts:49; the instrument is one test, budget spent on the built items
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts:289-292 case claim/idle -> outcome stopped
packages/kernel/src/job-settle.ts:49 o === "stopped" -> ending
